title: Two catalogues: Eve tools and installed business actions
alt: Discovery returns an action contract; invocation goes through separate authority checks.

title: How a non-Eve helper becomes running business code
alt: Imports, registries and routes connect source files to an actual request; arbitrary files are not automatically model tools.

title: A declared event with no executable conversion path
alt: Current Sales checkout event declaration reaches missing handler wiring; the responder stub does not persist a conversion.

title: A timeout after the provider has already acted
alt: The provider can complete a write before its response is lost; reconcile the outcome before safely retrying.

title: Three entry points share one booking implementation
alt: Patient tool, staff action and booking page reach shared booking code under different authority boundaries.

title: What the model sees and what the runtime executes
alt: Authored static and lifecycle-resolved tool definitions expose controlled schemas; code and framework defaults have separate roles.

title: One business setup contains many named actions [pack → capabilities]
alt: ClinicOS is the parent pack; clinic.find_times and clinic.book are two of its registered capabilities, alongside agents, Tables, screens and jobs.

title: One capability registry feeds the catalogue and the runtime
alt: A binding enters capabilities/implementations.ts, which supplies both generated entry.json metadata and the deployed invocation handler map.

title: Find an exact slot, then request its booking
alt: The clinic.find_times result supplies exact appointment fields to clinic.book, which previews, awaits approval, rechecks and confirms the provider outcome.
